titulo_es: Presente y pasado perfecto continuo: actividad y duración

texto: **Have/has been + verbo en -ing** conecta una actividad pasada con el presente: puede seguir en curso (**I've been waiting since six**) o haber terminado hace poco con un resultado visible (**I've been painting; my hands are dirty**). Usa **since** con el comienzo y **for** con la duración. Con verbos de estado como **know**, normalmente usa el presente perfecto simple: **I've known her for years**.

**Had been + verbo en -ing** enfoca una actividad y cuánto duraba hasta otro punto pasado: **I had been waiting for twenty minutes when the plumber arrived**. El contexto aclara si la actividad se detuvo o siguió después de ese punto.

frases.en: I've been renovating this flat since May.
frases.es: Llevo reformando este piso desde mayo.
analisis: desde mayo; la reforma continúa en el presente

frases.en: Last Thursday, the plumber arrived at ten.
frases.es: El jueves pasado, el fontanero llegó a las diez.

frases.en: I had been waiting for twenty minutes when he arrived.
frases.es: Llevaba veinte minutos esperando cuando llegó.

frases.en: The tap had been leaking for days, so I called him.
frases.es: El grifo llevaba días goteando, así que lo llamé.

frases.en: He fixed the tap, and I've been choosing new tiles since the repair.
frases.es: Arregló el grifo y llevo eligiendo baldosas nuevas desde la reparación.
analisis: desde ese momento pasado hasta ahora

bloques.pregunta: In “I've been renovating this flat since May”, what does the tense emphasise?

opciones.texto: The activity began in May and is still connected to the present.
opciones.explicacion: The sentence presents an ongoing renovation.

opciones.texto: A completed result with no connection to now.
opciones.explicacion: The continuous focuses on the activity, not only its completed result.

opciones.texto: An action that will start in May.
opciones.explicacion: **Since May** refers to a past starting point.

bloques.frase: I ___ been waiting for twenty minutes when the plumber arrived.

opciones.explicacion: Use **had been + -ing** for duration up to a past reference point.
This connects the activity to now, not the past arrival.
The past continuous does not use **been + -ing** in this pattern.

bloques.pregunta: How long had the narrator been waiting when the plumber arrived?

opciones.explicacion: The third line gives the duration up to the plumber's arrival.
That is how long the renovation has been going on.
The tap had been leaking for that period.

bloques.frase: The tap had been leaking for days.

opciones.explicacion: **Had been leaking** gives the duration up to a past point.
That would connect the duration to the present.
That does not express duration.

bloques.pregunta: In “I've been decorating since May” and “I've been decorating for two months”, what do the time phrases show?

opciones.texto: **Since May** gives the starting point; **for two months** gives the duration.
opciones.explicacion: **Since** + point in time; **for** + period of time.
**For two months** names a length of time.
**Since May** names when the activity began.

bloques.pregunta: Can the present perfect continuous describe an activity that has just stopped?

opciones.texto: Yes, when there is a present result or evidence of the recent activity.
opciones.explicacion: For example, **I've been painting; my hands are dirty**.

opciones.texto: No, it always means the activity is happening at this exact second.
opciones.explicacion: It can also describe a recently finished activity.
**Had been** refers to a past reference point.

bloques.frase: I've been choosing tiles ___ the repair.

opciones.explicacion: It refers to the starting point after the repair.
**For** would need a duration, such as **for two weeks**.
This does not fit the perfect continuous time phrase here.

bloques.pregunta: Which sentence uses a state verb naturally?

opciones.explicacion: **Know** is normally not used in the continuous form.

opciones.texto: I've been knowing her for years.
opciones.explicacion: Use the simple perfect with this state verb.

opciones.texto: I had been know her for years.
opciones.explicacion: This does not form a perfect continuous or simple perfect.

intro: El continuo perfecto destaca una actividad y su duración. El punto de referencia puede ser ahora o un momento pasado.
